answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20, Brady Hot Springs PoroTomo DAS, March 2016):

Coverage and detections:
- Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; 3.314% of the time span)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above the catalogue Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED estimate (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue magnitudes are calibrated, so this is the calibrated probability):
- b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198 (P(Mw>=5.5) over the observed volume = 5.236e-06; P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719)
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922 (observed-volume P = 0.0002155; P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809)
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474  (observed-volume P = 0.0006484; P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653)

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
- b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue probabilities indicate a very low likelihood of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event (at most ~1.5e-2 per year even for the lowest b = 0.65 scenario, and ~1.2e-4 per year at b = 1.0), while the DAS-based upper bound (0.07842/yr) is not calibrated and systematically over-counts because uncalibrated DAS detections are all treated as events above Mc.
